name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+24 partisan lean makes a Democratic win structurally improbable
Incumbent Nathaniel Moran holds an overwhelming fundraising edge ($2.4M raised vs. $33K for Yolanda Prince)
Prediction markets price the Republican win probability near 96%
No public polls or expert ratings exist; fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: This deep East Texas seat leans Republican by roughly 24 points, and Moran enters with incumbency, a nearly 70-to-1 fundraising advantage, and no outside spending against him. Markets price a Democratic upset at about 2 percent, and nothing in the evidence suggests moving materially off a 20-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development, such as a major scandal or a historic national wave, would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 1st District, anchored in Tyler and deep East Texas, leans Republican by roughly 24 points, and incumbent Nathaniel Moran is seeking re-election after winning the seat in 2022. He has raised about $2.4 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Yolanda Prince has raised about $33,000 with under $10,000 available. No outside groups are active on either side, and no public polls or expert ratings cover the race.

Prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 96 percent chance of holding the seat. With such a large financial gap, a heavily Republican electorate, and an incumbent running, this ranks among the safest Republican holds on the House map. The Democratic challenger would need a dramatic, unforeseen shift in the political environment to make the race competitive.
